summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish an independent guardian for unaccompanied non-citizen children in Australia and its external territories, with legal guardianship, advocacy and service oversight functions.
The guardian would arrange custody, promote suitable care and involve children in decisions, while removal from Australia would require the guardian’s prior written consent.
The defined group would be children under 18 arriving without visas and without specified adult relatives, with exclusions for certain family and permanent adoption circumstances.
changes: Removing a child from Australia without the required written consent would become a criminal offence.
Offences would also address removal from custodial arrangements and harbouring children removed from them.
Covered children could no longer be made wards of the Immigration Minister under the existing guardianship law.
The guardian would provide an annual report for presentation to Parliament.
summary.affected: Unaccompanied non-citizen children, their custodians and the guardian would be affected.
